entries.note: PMID 3543057 = Mojsov JCI 1987; quote verbatim in abstract. Note's 'only with glucose present' is a gloss (abstract reports 6.6 mM glucose, not glucose-dependence); untested holds.

PMID 8405741 resolves; quote verbatim (abstract). IV native GLP-1 is the endogenous ligand, not a drug of the class. First analog comparison is Kolterman 2003: 'The relative glucose and insulin concentration profiles were consistent with glucose-dependent insulinotropism.' Move same to 2003; keep 1993 in judgement.
PMID 10331407 = Young Diabetes 1999; quote and both ED50s (0.059 db/db, 0.25 rhesus) verbatim in abstract. untested holds.

PMID 12843147 resolves; quote verbatim (abstract). Same stands only under the v2 juxtaposition allowance: it compares ug/kg dose to animal ED50, not exposure. magnitude within_2x holds vs mouse only (monkey 0.25 vs 0.1 = 2.5x). Drop the 2005 fixed-dose aside (later knowledge).
Young 1999 abstract: quote verbatim; ZDF HbA1c fall, weight loss, weight ED50 1.0 ug/kg all stated. untested holds.

PMID 15504997 resolves; quote and -1.6 kg verbatim (abstract). NCT00039026 first posted 2002-06-10, no results (API). Same holds: primary endpoint matched; the weight and beta-cell misses are secondary, cross-drug (Larsen/Rolin = liraglutide at supraclinical dose) and belong in magnitude, not status.

Label PDF extracted locally (WebFetch could not parse it). Quote verbatim under 'Carcinogenesis, Mutagenesis, Impairment of Fertility'; 5/22/130x AUC and the 104-week mouse null (95x) confirmed. untested holds.

PMID 20203154 resolves; quote, primate GLP-1R, 20-month monkey and 2-yr calcitonin all in abstract. But source closes 'remain unknown' (source_calls_it should be null, not miss) and the 2010 label says relevance 'could not be ruled out'. Tumour endpoint untested until Pasternak 2024; contra moves there.

PMID 22338093 resolves; quote verbatim (abstract). Label 5.2 '7 cases ... 1 case (2.2 vs. 0.6 cases per 1000 patient-years)' confirmed from extracted PDF. Entry adds no status change; it inherits whatever safety 2 is scored. LEAD-3 registry date is a stand-in for pooled LEAD data.

missing: safety (C-cell, tumour endpoint): the first patient-level tumour comparisons are Bezin 2023 (doi:10.2337/dc22-1148; HR 1.58 all thyroid cancer, 1.78 MTC, supports the rat) and Pasternak 2024 (doi:10.1136/bmj-2023-078225; HR 0.93, 145,410 users, MTC CI wide). Under rule 5 the contra belongs at 2024 with Bezin as the dissent, not at 2010. Not re-opened within budget; the draft already cites both.

safety (calcitonin surrogate): Hegedus 2011 JCEM (doi:10.1210/jc.2010-2318), >5,000 liraglutide-treated subjects, 2-yr calcitonin null; a larger, non-abstract-only source for the 2010-era surrogate comparison than Bjerre Knudsen 2010. Not re-opened within budget.

safety (pancreatitis): LEADER (Marso 2016 NEJM, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1603827) reported acute pancreatitis 18 vs 23 in 9,340 patients; the three-species silence held in patients. Would be a same-type comparison in 2016 if the cell is not already contra. Not re-opened within budget.

efficacy (beta-cell durability): Bunck 2009/2011 Diabetes Care exenatide-vs-glargine washout studies are the human test of the Rolin 2002 beta-cell prediction; the draft says 'never demonstrable' where 'tested, not durable' may be the stricter reading. Not checked; lead only.
engagement: Kolterman 2003 (doi:10.1210/jc.2002-021545, already cited in dose) supplies the drug-of-class engagement quote; no new source needed.
rule_questions: Rule #26 (animals predicted harm that did not occur): the rat bioassay predicted C-cell tumours in 14-23% of females at 5-130x exposure; patients show flat calcitonin and no thyroid-cancer excess, but MTC is too rare for any human dataset to exclude a modest excess and the regulator wrote 'could not be ruled out'. Checker's call: untested until a patient tumour-endpoint comparison exists (2023/2024), then contra as a false positive, because the prediction was of a large effect that is excluded; 'conservative model doing its job' is a regulatory-utility argument, not a predictive-validity one, and the brief has no status for it. The year, not the status, is what the draft gets wrong.

Conflicting patient comparisons on the same endpoint (Bezin 2023 positive case-control vs Pasternak 2024 null cohort): the brief says contra overrides matched, but a positive-then-null sequence would read same(2023) -> contra(2024), which inverts the sense of contra. Needs a rule for which comparison governs when they disagree (study design? pooled?).

Is the endogenous ligand infused pharmacologically a 'drug of this class'? Checker's call: no. The atlas tracks drug development; native GLP-1(7-36)amide IV at 1.2 pmol/kg/min was never a product and its kinetics match no marketed agonist. Use the first analog (exenatide, Kolterman 2003). If the rule is mechanism-defined ('GLP-1 receptor agonists' includes the native agonist), the 1993 entry stands and this should be written down.

Primary endpoint matched, secondary prediction missed >5x (rat weight loss ~15% vs patient ~2%; beta-cell mass expansion never shown): checker's call is same with magnitude recorded; the brief has no 'right direction, wrong size' status, and contra is reserved for a wrong prediction on the question asked (disease response). Note the >5x figure is cross-drug (liraglutide 200 ug/kg bid in rats vs exenatide 10 ug bid in patients) and supraclinical, so it is not a clean miss either. If magnitude misses should be able to move status, the brief needs a threshold.

comparison_stated=false vs the checker rule 'same/contra with no published model-vs-patient comparison should be untested': the v2 drafter brief's comparison_stated field implies drafter juxtaposition is allowed for a status call (otherwise the field is redundant); the checker brief lists it as a failure. Engagement 2, dose 2 and efficacy 2 all depend on which governs. Checker applied the v2 allowance.

Duplicate-status entries: safety 3 (Nyborg 2012) changes no status and exists because the pancreatitis comparison was requested. 'One entry per change of status' either forbids it or the brief should say when an extra comparison entry is allowed.
